To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
psychotropic medication is frequently prescribed in nursing homes and that psychopharmacologic drug use is associated with an increase in mortality and morbidity in the long-term care setting

the majority of the geriatric psychiatrists and the majority of the homes for the elderly in Germany are satisfied with the psychopharmacologic therapy in homes for the elderly and that the majority of homes for the elderly have a written policy for psychopharmacologic medication in homes for the old.
the psychopharmacologic drug treatment in homes for the elderly and nursing homes has increased over the past years and is now at a level of 40%.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: 1. The current psychotropic medication practice in homes for aged and nursing homes. 2. The current psychopathological symptomatology in homes for aged. 3. The relationship between psychopathological symptoms and the current medication.
the following questions: (a) Which psychopharmacological agents are prescribed in homes for the elderly and nursing homes? (b) How often are these agents prescribed in the various types of homes?

the following questions: What are the most common psychopharmacologic treatments in geriatric psychosomatic medicine? What are the reasons for the choice of a certain drug? Which drugs are used for which indication? What is the frequency of polypharmacotherapy? What is the quality of psychopharmacological treatment?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
geriatric psychiatry is a medical specialty which is not only a part of the medical care system, but also a part of the social system.
the psychopharmacologic therapy is not yet established in homes for the elderly and nursing homes.
gerontopsychiatric treatment in nursing homes has to be improved and that there are still deficits in the pharmacological treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
geriatric psychiatrists are needed to provide geropsychiatric competence in homes for the elderly.
psychopharmacologic therapy in the homes for the elderly and nursing homes is still a major challenge.
psychopharmacological competence in gerontopsychiatry should be the basis for all psychotropic medication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to be more careful about the way we use and interpret the data we generate from these studies.
the current practice of psychopharmacology in the care of elderly patients is not satisfactory.
the use of the term "geriatric" in the context of psychopharmacology is a misnomer.
